instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to design a Verilog module that implements a Hamming code encoder and decoder. 
A Hamming code is a type of error-correcting code that can detect and correct single-bit errors in data. 
The encoder takes a block of k data bits and adds n-k parity bits to produce a block of n code bits. 
The decoder takes a block of n code bits and uses the parity bits to detect and correct any single-bit errors.

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of k input signals (in1, in2, ..., ink)
Outputs: a set of n output signals (out1, out2, ..., outn)

Your module should implement the following functionality:

Encoder:
The encoder should take the k input signals and use them to compute the n-k parity bits using the following algorithm:
- Determine the positions of the parity bits (i.e., the positions that are powers of 2)
- Set the parity bits to the XOR of the data bits that have a 1 in their binary representation at the corresponding position
- Concatenate the data bits and parity bits to produce the n code bits

Decoder:
The decoder should take the n code bits and use them to detect and correct any single-bit errors using the following algorithm:
- Determine the positions of the parity bits (i.e., the positions that are powers of 2)
- Compute the parity of the bits at each parity position
- If a parity error is detected, flip the corresponding bit
- Extract the k data bits from the corrected code bits

To implement the Hamming code encoder and decoder, you should use Verilog code to define the parity bit positions and the XOR functions used to compute the parity bits. 
You should then use these functions to connect the inputs to the encoder and the decoder, and to compute the corrected output signals in the decoder.
